title: Cautious surge mitigation and tenant pin notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for a conservative rollout pattern focused on managing sudden traffic surges while preserving per-tenant control (tenant pinning). This is an experimental checklist + decision tree I want to try for next week’s model flip where we expect several large tenants to hit bursty traffic.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Target rollout: flip hosted default from model v2.3-q8 to v2.4-quant (smaller but untested in high-concurrency).
- We have per-tenant routing keys and a soft-traffic-steering layer that can pin requests by tenant_id.
- Metrics available in Console: p50/p95 latency, token-per-second, 5m error rate (4xx/5xx), quality-sampled evals (periodic).
- Recovery knobs: change routing policy, pin tenant to older model, throttle requests via quota, divert region, increase dedicated burst pool (if on Dedicated).

TL;DR (how I'll run it)
1) Start a micro-canary: 0.1% global traffic but include a small set of tenants (two enterprise tenants + internal QA bot).
2) Observe 30 minutes steady-state. If p95 latency delta < 15% and error rate delta < 0.25ppt, increase to 1% and include 5 more tenants.
3) If any tenant shows sustained p95 delta > 25% or token-dropbacks, pin that tenant back immediately and go to incident template.

Selection of initial tenants:
- criteria: tenants with predictable traffic, small request size, and willing to be in early canary (ops-approved).
- picks: tenant_alpha (internal), tenant_beta (staging partner), tenant_gamma (small enterprise).
- include a synthetic traffic generator (qa-bot) to exercise edge lengths and streaming.

Checklist (pre-rollout)
- [ ] Ensure canary config is uploaded: routing policy name = "cautious-surge-2026-03"
- [ ] Create tenant pin recipes for the three initial tenants (TTL 24h, manual-unpin).
- [ ] Create dashboard: compare model v2.3-q8 vs v2.4-quant p50/p95, 5m error rate, token throughput, memory pressure on nodes.
- [ ] Add alert rule (channel = #deploy-runbooks): p95 increase > 20% for 10m OR 5m error rate increase > 0.5ppt.
- [ ] Run a dry-run with traffic generator in staging (10k reqs) and snapshot logs.
- [ ] Notify CS contacts for the selected tenants and include rollback contact list.

Canary step sizes (suggested)
- Step 0: 0.1% global, three tenants (internal + 2 small) — 30 min watch
- Step 1: 1% global, +5 selected low-risk tenants — 1 hour watch
- Step 2: 5% global, include mid-range tenants — 2 hour watch
- Step 3: 20% global, open to all non-enterprise — 4 hour watch
- Step 4: full gradual -> proceed with traffic-steering plan to finish in 24–48h

Signals to watch (primary)
- Latency: p95 (client-perceived) absolute and % delta vs baseline (v2.3-q8).
- Error surface: 5m 5xx rate, 4xx spikes (client-side validation issues), stream truncation events.
- Throughput: tokens/s and token drop events from the runtime (OOM/backpressure).
- Quality: eval set pass-rate (sampled); if coverage drops > 6% raise caution.
- Infra: GPU mem pressure, swap events, scheduler queue length.

Decision thresholds (my conservative defaults)
- Soft caution: p95 delta > 15% for 15m OR 5m 5xx increase > 0.25ppt -> pause progression and investigate.
- Hard stop & rollback: p95 delta > 25% for 10m OR 5m 5xx increase > 1.0ppt OR any persistent client-facing data corruption/regression -> pin affected tenants and roll back globally if > 10% traffic impacted.

Immediate actions on a signal (playbook)
1) Narrow scope: identify affected tenant(s) via request traces and route mappings.
2) Pin affected tenant(s) to previous model via tenant-pin API (command below).
3) If surge is infrastructure-related (node OOM/backpressure), divert new incoming traffic to other region or scale Dedicated burst pool: trigger infra-autoscale request.
4) If quality regressions (evals fail), pause rollout, open a short RC: revert model build and create a hotfix branch.
5) Notify (#deploy-runbooks, CS on-call). Create an incident ticket if escalation needed.

Quick commands (examples)
- Pin tenant to previous model (curl):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/pin \n    -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant_alpha","model":"v2.3-q8","reason":"canary rollback - latency spike","ttl_secs":86400}'

- Unpin tenant (manual):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/unpin -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant_alpha"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'

- Increase canary global fraction (admin CLI):
  rwdctl rollout set-fraction --name cautious-surge-2026-03 --fraction 0.01

Telemetry playbook (what to collect quickly)
- First 10m: detailed traces for all requests from canary tenants (sample 100%).
- Next 50m: aggregated p50/p95 buckets, per-tenant error histograms, and runtime GC/queue metrics every 1m.
- Keep a rolling log snippet attached to the incident for 72h after any pin.

Decision tree (ascii, rough):
 Start
  |
  +-- Observe metrics for 30m
       |
       +-- metrics OK -> increase to next step
       |
       +-- metrics show p95 delta > 15% -> isolate tenant(s)
             |
             +-- affects single tenant -> pin tenant and continue for others
             |
             +-- affects >10% traffic OR infra OOM -> rollback global to v2.3-q8 and trigger postmortem

Notes on tenant pin semantics (implementation reminders)
- Pin is sticky per tenant session until TTL expires or manual unpin. Must ensure SDKs respect tenant header precedence.
- Pin overrides route-level fallback; confirm fallback still triggers for capacity overflow.
- For multi-tenant requests (e.g., batch calls), use the originating tenant as key. Document corner case.

Surge mitigation controls (ordered by preference)
1) Pin specific tenant(s) to stable model (least disruptive to others).
2) Apply per-tenant quota throttling (soft 429s) for noisy tenants.
3) Divert traffic regionally if localized nodes saturated.
4) Activate Dedicated burst pool (if contract allows).
5) Global rollback (last resort).

Post-change checklist (quick)
- [ ] Confirm pins applied for affected tenants and visible in Console
- [ ] Save snapshots of dashboards and traces
- [ ] File a short postmortem note with root cause and timeline (template: one-paragraph RCA + timeline + follow-ups)
- [ ] Schedule a short sync with CS for any impacted customers

Open questions / TODOs (personal)
- TODO: add a test-case to the canary harness that simulates token-burst patterns (long prompt + short replies) to validate KV cache behavior under v2.4 quant path.
- TODO: confirm that pin TTL doesn't interact badly with SDK local caching (risk: SDK may keep using model hint until restart).
- Question: should we allow auto-unpin after 1h if metrics improve vs leaving 24h TTL? Pros/cons: auto-unpin reduces manual ops but may re-expose tenant unexpectedly. Leaning towards manual unpin.
- Follow-up: sync with infra to add a fast-scaling trigger for Dedicated burst pool in emergency (response < 5min).

My immediate plan:
- Run staging dry-run today (10k synthetic).
- If clean, schedule first micro-canary tomorrow morning (low traffic window).
- Keep this scratchpad open during the run and convert to a proper runbook postmortem.

Random notes to self:
- Keep a copy of the pin command in SRE's incident template for speed.
- If a tenant is pinned 3+ times in 30 days, propose a tenant-specific SLA conversation with CS about stability expectations.

----
End of scratchpad. Will refine after the dry-run.
